 USDA mass reorganization plan remains on hold
 The American Federation of Government Employees has been suing USDA over the reorganization plans, warning that the effort will lead to mass staff attrition.
 Michele Sandiford 
 November 9, 2026 2:05 pm 
 < a min read 
 The Agriculture Department’s mass reorganization plan will have to remain on hold. A federal judge has denied USDA’s request to stay an injunction that’s been keeping those plans paused since mid-October. While denying the agency’s motion, the judge is also ordering both parties in the lawsuit to hold a meeting to discuss a proposed clarification of the stay order. The American Federation of Government Employees has been suing USDA over the reorganization plans, warning that the effort will lead to mass staff attrition. 
-- Drew Friedman 
 ( Court documents - AFGE v. USDA) 
 The cloud security program known as FedRAMP is ready to kick off its final set of certification pilots. Vendors can now submit applications to FedRAMP for the 20x Class D pilot for high-assurance certifications for cloud services. The program management office started accepting applications in October from companies that want to get into the final set of test cases. The Class D pilot includes 10 new security indicators, two new definitions and updates to six different rule sets compared with the Class C requirements. FedRAMP says it may add key security indicators or rules during the pilot based on feedback from vendor participants. The last day to apply for the Class D pilot is Nov. 19. 
-- Jason Miller 
 ( FedRAMP is ready to kick off its final set of certification pilots - FedRAMP ) 
 The Department of Homeland Security is not conducting as many inspections at its detention facilities, even as DHS puts more people in immigration custody. In a new report, the Government Accountability Office details how DHS’s detention facility inspections dipped last year. That’s partially because DHS cut most staff at the Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman in 2025. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Office of Detention Oversight also decreased the frequency of its inspections last year. Meanwhile, the population of noncitizens detained by ICE grew by more than 50% between April 2025 and April 2026. 
-- Justin Doubleday 
 ( GAO: Changes in inspections of ICE facilities raise questions about oversight - Government Accountability Office)

 More individuals and businesses took advantage of digital services provided by the IRS for the last filing season. The tax agency reported that for fiscal 2025, more than 37 million individual users filed through the individual online account platform, a 34% increase over 2024. The number of tax professionals using IRS services increased by 57%. Additionally, the IRS says 12% more citizens received refunds through direct deposit. Overall, the IRS collected a record $5.6 trillion in taxes last year, which was 5% more than in 2024. 
-- Jason Miller 
 ( IRS sees boon in digital services for 2025 filing season - Internal Revenue Service) 
 The Federal Aviation Administration is no longer using floppy disks across several airports. The move is a part of the FAA's air traffic control system modernization efforts. The Enterprise Information Display System, or E-IDS, replaces four legacy systems from the 1980s across 400 FAA facilities. The E-IDS is a digital display that pulls relevant operational information into one place. Air traffic controllers will use E-IDS to quickly see updates, status information and other alerts. The FAA also says the new system will reduce costly repairs and workarounds while enhancing flight safety. The FAA plans to install E-IDS at 435 sites by the end of 2028. 
-- Silvia Oakland 
 ( FAA retires floppy disks as a part of agency wide modernization - Federal Aviation Administration ) 
 The Education Department says it’s already seeing success with a new tool for combating fraud. Earlier this year, Education’s Office of Federal Student Aid started using a Real-Time Fraud Detection Capability as part of the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, or FAFSA. Speaking at a webinar last week, Richard Lucas, acting chief operating officer at FSA, said the tool is on track to prevent $1.2 billion in student aid fraud. Education says the tool allows “legitimate students to proceed through the FAFSA process quickly, while requiring a small portion of applicants to complete additional steps to confirm their identity as part of the online FAFSA submission process.” 
-- Justin Doubleday 
 ( CMS, Education tout data driven fraud prevention savings - Federal News Network) 
 The Space Force is standing up a new operations center for the Space Data Network Backbone program. The center will serve as a hub for integrating disparate satellite systems and managing data transport across multiple providers. Space Force Lt. Col. Alexa Eggert said standing up the center is “a crucial step in maturing the Space Data Network into a fully operational, multi-vendor capability.” Space Systems Command awarded Viasat a contract with a maximum ceiling of $450 million to “design, field and scale” the center. 
-- Anastasia Obis 
 ( Space Force stands up operations center to expand data network backbone - U.S. Space Systems Command) 
 The effort to launch a governmentwide HR IT system is making headway. After a major contract award to Oracle in June, the Office of Personnel Management is pushing forward with the implementation phase of the new platform. “We have actually a system in our lower environments that we’re actively configuring. We are integrating with three of the payroll providers actively now — we’re testing with two of them already,” Bridget Dongarra, OPM’s core HCM program manager, said during a Nov. 6 conference hosted by ACT-IAC. OPM has also kicked off work with all 11 “wave one” agencies that will be first to integrate with the new system. They’re expected to onboard during 2027. 
-- Drew Friedman 
 ( Update on OPM’s HR IT initiative - Office of Personnel Management, ACT-IAC) 
 Department of Government Efficiency acting Administrator Amy Gleason says the next phase of America.gov is on its way. In coming updates, America.gov will provide users with an authenticated experience. The website will also use an artificial intelligence agent to help citizens complete forms or retrieve information. As a final step to updating the website, citizens and other users will use a dashboard to understand the status of their government request. 
-- Silvia Oakland 
 ( DOGE Acting Administrator teases next phase of America.gov - Federal News Network) 
 The Army’s $50 billion Marketplace for the Acquisition of Professional Services contract is facing another round of bid protests as the service works to finalize the massive contracting vehicle. The Government Accountability Office recommended that the Army allow small businesses to submit offers as teams and reopen the competition to give companies time to submit new or revised bids after industry challenged the solicitation’s prohibition on small businesses forming teaming arrangements. The Army reopened the competition to let small businesses bid on the contract, but two companies now argue that the revised solicitation still restricts their ability to compete. Another company is challenging the terms of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification requirements. 
-- Anastasia Obis 
 ( Army’s MAPS contract hit with new obstacles - Federal News Network)
